articleTitle: Modeling and simulation of first-order Li-Ion battery cell with experimental validation
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper the first-order RC equivalent circuit model (ECM) of the Lithium Ion cell is presented. This circuit can be used in real-time applications, for example, the battery management system (BMS) because is not computational complex. The model parameters are identified with experimental measurements on a real Li-Ion cell. First the discharge capacity was measured and after the cell was completely charged and discharged applying constant current pulses to determine the open circuit voltage (VOC) and the parameters for the equivalent circuit components. For one ECM the parameters are calculated using one discharge pulse which was applied at approximatively 60% state of charge and for the second model the circuit parameters are calculated for each discharge pulse and saved in a look-up-table depending on the state of charge. For model validation was applied a charge/discharge scenario and the results show a good agreement between the battery voltage and the ECM voltage.

articleTitle: An Efficient Peer-to-Peer Based Blokchain Approach for Prosumers Energy Trading in Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The pressure of climate change and the need to adopt renewable energy sources (RES) have led to an increased development of microgrid technologies. Their modularizable and scalable nature presents opportunities for the development of a new class of players in the power system, i.e. prosumers. The large-scale integration of RES creates acute challenges to the existing power systems. In this context, a reliable and secured balance between energy generation and consumption is highly required. To overcome these problems at microgrid level, a key role is played by the peer-to-peer energy trading using the blockchain concept. In this paper, we present an efficient approach that can be useful for energy trading using blockchain from both active participants (prosumers and consumers). The proposed approach meets the new Romanian regulation regarding prosumers. The results of the study emphasize that the proposed methodology could lead to an efficient balance between local supply and demand with benefits to the participants.

articleTitle: Electric vehicle Carbon footprint reduction via intelligent charging strategies
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In recent years, electric vehicles (EVs) are seen as an effective solution to the arising environmental and sustainability concerns related to the transportation sector. As opposed to conventional vehicles, EVs do not entail tailpipe emission of CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and other ambient air pollutants and require lower operational cost. However, the benefits that EVs can bring highly depend on their charging strategy. Moreover, the ever-increasing deployment of EVs on a global scale, and their uncontrolled charging (currently predominant) requirements, can cause significant burden for national grids and local distribution networks. The solutions EV could bring depend on the adopted charging strategies, i.e. dump charging, smart charging or V2G. This paper compares various EV charging strategies at the UK national level in perspective to 2030 and 2040 targets. This study clearly shows the benefits EVs could bring if their charging is intelligently controlled, resulting in a more positive impact on electricity distribution grids, a higher integration of renewable energy sources (RES) and lower CO2 emissions.

articleTitle: Delay Compensation in the PMSM Control by using a Smith Predictor
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This article presents a structure for speed control in a PMSM drive by compensating the effect of the delay fed into the control loop by the speed sensor (Tachogenerator) by using a Smith Predictor. The inner loop for current and torque control follows the general lines of the FOC (Field Oriented Control) strategy in terms of describing the motor operation equations in d-q model on rotor reference frame (after using the Clark and Park transformations), and obtaining a maximum torque by setting the reference current to zero on d-axis. The control system is a cascade system where the speed control system is the outer loop, and the fixed part is the inner loop for current control together with the PMSM. For the modeling of the fixed part, 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> and 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order continuous and discrete transfer functions are presented, to which the delay block is added. Good results were obtained after the simulations where the transfer function is of the 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order, by compensating the delay effect. Considering that the usual delay fed by the speed sensor is lower than the maximum delay compensated by the proposed structure, and the control used is of common PI type with anti-windup, the results of simulations recommend the implementation into a real time embedded system.

articleTitle: UAV development and impact in the power system
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The use of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), or drones, in the energy sector is at the beginning, with many companies still unsure about the value the drones could bring to their operations. But this market segment is fast-growing with a potentially bright future. Drones can improve efficiency, speed, safety and cost from the design, pre-construction and development stages through to commissioning and ongoing maintenance. The main applications for drones can be in: asset inventory, construction and repairs, maintenance management, emissions monitoring, solar and wind power inspections, inspection of power lines and component parts. Energy transmission and distribution networks are strategic assets that need a rigorous maintenance strategy to maintain their reliability, availability and sustainability. While numerous tools and methods already exist for power line inspection and maintenance tasks, the UAV's are slowly proving that they offer a practical and valuable approach. This paper presents the regulatory framework, the main applications in the electropower system and the safety and security concerns related to the use of drones.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence Techniques for Fault Location and Detection in Distributed Generation Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: There are multiple reasons that distributed generation systems are exposed to faults and errors. Among them we can consider the most common ones being failure of the power system components or lighting strikes. Power system failure is usually caused by components failure, human error or equipment aging. The above-mentioned events affect the power system reliability and imply expensive repairs, lost of productivity and dissatisfied customers. Due to the fact that faults are unpredictable, fast fault location and isolation is necessary to minimize the impact of fault in distribution systems. Therefore, many methods have been previously developed by researchers to locate and detect these faults in distribution power systems that incorporate distributed generation. The main available methods can be split into two categories: conventional and artificial intelligence techniques. Conventional methods are composed of travelling wave method and impedance-based method while artificial intelligence techniques include Artificial Neural Network, Support Vector Machine, Fuzzy Logic, Genetic Algorithm and matching approach. However, fault detection using intelligent methods are difficult to implement due to the fact that it requires training data for processing and also are time consuming. This paper presents some of the newly introduced artificial intelligence techniques for islanding detection in distributed generation power networks. Research works in islanding detection, control algorithms, advantages and disadvantages are presented, hence the opportunities in islanding detection research area in power distribution system can be explored further.

articleTitle: The Construction of a Wireless Power Supply System using Planar Spiral Inductors
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The wireless power systems are becoming increasingly used for a wide range of applications. The wireless charge of newest gadgets is a new technology in all the world in our days. The purpose of this paper is to design such a system using planar spiral inductors. The planar spiral inductors have a wide range of applications in industry. The planar spiral inductors, that will be used to design the wireless power supply system, are first modeled to extract their parameters. The inductors are parametric analyzed to optimal design and the optimized spiral inductors are practical constructed. Finally, they are used to design and construct a wireless power supply system.

articleTitle: Monitoring Solar Panels using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Increasing photovoltaic (PV) park installations, in conjunction with the development of wind farms and other renewable energy systems, is a safe way to reduce carbon dioxide emissions that are accused of having led to significant climate change in recent years. Photovoltaic cells must operate in open space in order to capture solar radiation with the disadvantage of being continuously exposed to meteorological phenomena. The effects of some of these phenomena can lead to degradation of photovoltaic panel efficiency or operation. In this paper we propose a method of monitoring photovoltaic panels for the identification of possible degradation of operation based on machine learning (ML) techniques. The development of the model and its validation is based on data collected both from the panels' photovoltaic control system and weather data collected from Internet.

articleTitle: Sorting System for e-Waste Recycling using Contour Vision Sensors
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Recycling old electronic components facilitates the recovery of valuable materials that can be used to produce new ones. As a result, energy is saved, pollution and greenhouse gas emissions are reduced, and many natural resources are salvaged by extracting fewer raw materials. The paper focuses on rapid sorting method developed for separating the dismembered components of a personal computers motherboard. After a simultaneous disassembly process of the board, some of the components like plastics, silicon chips, surface-mount devices and magnetic components need to be intelligently sorted, therefore economically separated. In the sorting process a conveyor belt was used to transport the components one by one. A contour vision sensor was used to acquire and process the images, consequently to recognize the components. The visual sensor binary code output is connected to a Mitsubishi FX3G programmable logic controller. Finally, electro pneumatic valves with directional air flow control are used to position the objects from the conveyor belt into separate bins.

articleTitle: Electromobility and Climate Change
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: At the moment, the generalization of electric transportation creates the fear that this will increase both global warming and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> pollution generated from power plants using fossil fuels as a result of increased electricity demand. The paper analyzes the real situation in Romania and abroad in terms of pollution sources and the modern methods that our society will provide in the near future: energy storage in batteries and the massive recycling the waste battery materials.

articleTitle: Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for the Evaluation of the Demand Response in the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca Buildings
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The concept of Demand Response (DR) is not really widespread across Romania, so the Technical University of Cluj-Napoca (TUCN) implemented a pilot project in its own buildings within the Horizon 2020, named DR-BOB (project no. 696114/2016). Within this project, the Romanian demonstration site implemented different DR events throughout the whole evaluation period. The Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) are calculated for each DR event and on the entire evaluation year. This paper reflects the evaluation of the pilot sites, focusing on description of calculation method of the KPIs and the results obtained at the Swimming Pool Complex. The KPIs are calculated in accordance with the methodology defined in [6].

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach for NILM based on Odd Harmonic Current Vectors
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper examines the application of machine learning techniques in NILM methodologies based on the first three odd harmonic order current vectors as the only attributes of the appliances. Proper formulation of the measured current waveform of appliances' combinations is also presented. We apply our methodology on performed measurements of typical Low Voltage residential installations considering harmonic order currents as the input features for both the training and disaggregation scheme. Our results support the hypothesis that the identification performance is enhanced when higher harmonic currents are included in the NILM methodology.

articleTitle: Determination of Optimum Tilt Angle for Fixed Photovoltaic Modules in Iasi, Romania
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The energy output of a photovoltaic system is significantly affected by the variability of the incident solar radiation. Thus, increasing the incident solar radiation is one of the most important solution which can be implemented to increase the output of such PV systems. This can be achieved by installing the PV panels on sun tracking systems. However, these trackers are expensive and most of the photovoltaic power plants are using fixed PV modules. In this paper the optimum tilt angle of the fixed PV panels in analyzed as noticeable gains in terms of energy output can be achieved by using a variable tilt angle over the year.

articleTitle: Over Grid Connection of Non Dispatchable Utility Photovoltaic Power Plants in Romania
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Modern world runs on energy. Energy is the raw material needed to power the engine of economic development for any country in the world. Today it is worldwide recognized that using nonrenewable sources is changing the Earth's climate in a negative direction. Given these climate-change threats, renewable energies appear to be the wave of the future. European States, including Romania, introduced programs for limiting CO2 emissions and supporting renewable energy development. Renewable based power plants, such as photovoltaic (PV), wind and biomass have flourished all over Europe and around the world. New interconnections requirements for utility-connected power plants based on renewable sources are coming into force in European countries, responsible for supporting the grid operation and stability. This paper presents an example of technical compliance certification test procedure of non-dispatchable utility photovoltaic power plants. The mandatory technical conditions and the tests carried out in order to certify technical compliance with national regulations are describe and illustrate. Practical results illustrating the photovoltaic power plant behavior are presented. This example may be configured as a tutorial chapter for specialists in the field of power systems engineering interested in designing, powering, connecting to the grid and operating photovoltaic power plants.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis Between the PI Speed Controller and Two-Degrees-of-Freedom Speed Controller for Induction Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: We present in this paper a comparative study between a PI speed controller and the two-degree-of-freedom (2DOF) speed controller, used in a sensorless vector control system with direct orientation after the rotor flux. The simultaneous estimation of the speed and rotor flux is done by using an extended Gopinath Observer (EGO). Comparative analysis is performed by using simulation in the Matlab-Simulink programming environment.

articleTitle: A Solution for Studying the D.C. Motor Control Using NI MyRIO-1900
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Today, in industry, electrical motor is a very important element for mobile robots and autonomous systems. The virtual instrumentation and embedded myRIO devices are very useful tools for didactic purpose and understanding the working principles of the electrical motors control. In this paper, the authors propose a solution for DC motor speed controlling and monitoring. For this, an application was created in the LabVIEW programming graphical environment which is running on NI MyRIO-1900 configurable equipment. This application highlights that the embedded device can be easily integrated into a teaching lab.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transmission — State of the Art and Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper are analyzed the main methods of wireless transmission of electrical energy, as well as their applications. For the beginning, there is a brief history of the development of the wireless electric power transmission technology. There are presented the principles of functioning of the main methods of wireless transmission of electrical energy, as well as the technical problems that need to be solved in the future. There are also presented the main applications of this technology, as well as the main companies that produce commercial wireless electrical power transmission equipment. Finally, we present the future opportunities of these wireless power transmission technologies and recommendations for future research topics in this field.

articleTitle: Noise and vibration analysis of an in-wheel motor with integrated magnetic gear dedicated for light electric application
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper describes first, a structural behavior of a permanent magnet synchronous machine, with inversed structure Above its topology it is placed a magnetic gear which has the role to increase the speed of the machine. The main purpose of this structure is to offer the possibility to obtain different levels of torque and speed from the two available rotors. In this paper is presented the vibro-acoustic behavior of the studied structure. It is known that the cause for the noise in a machine is due to the vibrations produced mainly by the radial forces within the structure. Because of the complexity of the structure, the main parts are studied individually to observe the level of noise produced of each one of them, separately. The comparison between numerical results of noise and vibration made for the two stators and two rotors represent the consistency of the paper.

articleTitle: Contributions to monitoring the condition of substations
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: By promoting modern and competitive techniques and equipment for online monitoring and diagnosis, it is possible to track natural or accidental degradation over time. If identified in time and remedied, it will not generate serious events which may be sources of extremely costly damage for electric power suppliers and consumers. At the same time it is possible to extend the life of the equipment, optimize the maintenance program and reduce the outages and expenses for planned repairs. The paper presents an analysis of the vital parameters of MV, LV transformer substations and proposes a system for monitoring their working condition. The main objective of the paper is to present a modular system for transformer substation monitoring in order to increase the quality of electric power supply for consumers and reduce the costs of equipment overhaul and maintenance. Based on the considerations on the transformation substation condition monitoring, the paper presents achieved of such a monitoring system, which can be integrated into SCADA.

articleTitle: Achieving interoperability of power system protection using SCADA and PMU information
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Protection system relying on SCADA information is the cornerstone of transmission system operation. Recently, phasor measurement units have been deployed on a wider scale and several applications based on the synchronized measurement information are developed. Based on the Romanian policy regarding Smart Grid deployment, in this paper a proposal for information exchange between existing SCADA and the newly deployed synchrophasor measurement system is presented. Both the physical and communication layers SCADA-PDC-PMUs are described. Data exchange protocol needs to fulfill both protection requirements for each system element and for the dispatching center, in order to achieve the EMS-SCADA functionalities. It is underlined the importance of achieving interoperability using as example the state estimation routinely performed by the TSO. It is described a platform for data and information exchange where new logical blocks are integrated for achieving fast protection functionalities using the synchronized information provided by PMUs. The paper concludes with practical recommendations and future work.

articleTitle: Step by step Limiting for Capacitors Inrush Current Used in Voltage Power Supplies
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: A voltage power supply needs filter capacitors to deliver a constant output value. The bigger the power supply, bigger become capacitors, so to connect them into circuit there must be a limitation to avoid inrush current. A step by step current limitation implies connecting multiple capacitors in steps.

articleTitle: Management System for the Control of the Forklifts Activity in a Factory
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper presents a management system based on IoT devices for controlling the forklifts at a factory. The engine optimization system proposed by the authors consists of a location server, a warehouse management server, and several devices mounted on a forklift truck that are connected to an Internet of Things wireless network and which have RFID readers. The location server, using the wireless network, manages to determine the position of each device and, depending on it, and on the information it has from the warehouse management server, will send various actions that the operator of the forklift will execute, thus reducing the distances covered by the forklift and thus reducing the handling and loading times, reducing the energy consumption and optimizing the work of the forklift truck operators.

articleTitle: Fault Analysis of a High Voltage Direct Current Link Using Detailed Equivalent Models for Modular Multilevel Converters
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The scope of the paper is to present a detailed analysis of different submodule topologies, which can address DC faults, using detailed equivalent models. These models allow a thorough look starting from the submodule level and moving higher to the converter level. Consequently, having such flexibility in analyzing the high voltage direct current modular multilevel converter also allows a good DC fault analysis.

articleTitle: Analysis of Integration of PV Power Plant in Railway Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Due to the large and rapid fluctuation of requested power, the coupling between renewable energy and tramway system can be affected by serious control problems. Therefore, the use of an energy storage system is required in order to store and optimally dispatch the energy. Supercapacitors (SC) are the well suitable technology for traction applications but are limited by the energy density. The use of “hybrid” SC and battery storage systems permits to supply the peak power and recovery energy by braking with SC; instead the integration with renewable energy can be optimized with the batteries. The paper proposes an optimal design for the reduction of cost of battery storage systems integrated with photovoltaic power plants.

articleTitle: Numeric Simulator for the Analysis of Transients due to Fault in Electric Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The objective of the paper is to create a numerical simulator for three-phase circuits related to medium voltage power systems. Numerical Simulator allows the elimination of the difficulties encountered made in the analysis of regimes transients caused by faults. Several types of faults can be analyzed using the virtual simulator conceived by us. This paper is concerned with the numeric simulation of transient regimes produced in an electric distribution network, caused by a double grounding and by broken conductor grounded towards the consumer. Several parameters are used for the determination of their importance in the evolution of the transient, such as: the initial phase of the voltage at the faulty place, the grounding resistance at the faulty place and the method used for grounding the neutral point of the electric network.

articleTitle: Sensorless Control of Multi-Motors BLDC using Back-EMF Observer
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This article presents a BLDC multi-motor sensorless control system with rigid coupling. The control systems of each motor are achieved in cascade, where the external speed loop includes a PI controller, and the inner loop includes an on-off hysteresis controller. The rotor position is estimated by using a back-EMF observer. The back-EMF observer provides both the rotor speed and the commutation signals used in the inverter commands. The main task of the BLDC motor master and slave control systems is to maintain the same speed of the master and slave motors with the reference, and to generate the electromagnetic torque for each motor according to the torque required by the load when the load is distributed both as balanced and unbalanced for the two motors. The main functional blocks in the Simulink implementation are described, along with the control parameters. Real-time implementation of the BLDC multi-motor sensorless control system with rigid coupling is recommended by the good results obtained from numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Automated 3D Scanner for Electromagnetic Radiation Assessment near the WPT Active Part
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The proposed paper describes the development of a high resolution measurement system for the electromagnetic radiations emitted by the active element of a wireless power transmitter, WPT. This system consists of a spatial manipulator for the 3D-fieldsensor and an advanced board for its signal acquisition and processing, both managed by the microcontroller and computer applications. The main goal of this contribution is to experimentally validate the spatial field distribution in order to optimize the location of the emitter-receiver WPT coils. The resultant values were obtained around a fixed frequency, identical to the nominal frequency of a commercial WPT, approx. 150 kHz. The used flexible structure has advantages in terms of accurate radiation mapping in the vicinity of the active element, while also contributing to time reducing for the measurement process.

articleTitle: Influence of soil resistivity on substations earth grounding system
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper emphasizes the variation of the grounding resistance for the components of the earth grounding, depending on the nature of the soil, that is based on the soil resistivity. It also presents the variation of the touch and step voltage values according to the same resistivity of the soil. The study can be expanded, making a database of table with results, allowing a quick reading of touch and step voltages for different configurations of substations and different soil types.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling and Parametric Analysis of a Switched Reluctance Motor
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents the numerical modeling of a switched reluctance motor / generator use in the automotive traction industry. The performance, efficiency and top-of-the-line features of reluctance machines combined with its, robust low cost construction make this technology an attractive alternative to other types of engines typically selected for traction applications. In this research, a variation of the model geometric and supply current for a switched reluctance motor / generator was made for applications in complete hybrid vehicles.

articleTitle: Evaluating the Performances of Electric Waveforms Analysis Relying on the Stationary Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The extraction from distorted electric waveforms of the instantaneous components oscillating at the fundamental frequency must be characterized by accuracy and efficiency related to computational resources (memory and runtime). When the Stationary Wavelet Transform (SWT) is employed, these performances are affected by the sampling rate of the data acquisition system used to acquire the waveforms, the topology of the decomposition tree (number of components in the root nodes and number of levels) and the wavelet mother. This paper is dedicated to an original methodology conceived to deduce the optimal parameters required to provide an accurate and efficient operational context for the analysis relying on SWT. The studies are focused on three data acquisition systems characterized by different sampling rates, used by authors. A systematic procedure dedicated to parameters deducing is presented and validated on simulated and experimental signals. Comparative studies are provided as well.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Price Coupling Mechanism in the Day Ahead Electricity Markets
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The electricity price variation on the spot market and the electricity price increase in recent times are subject to controversy due to the incomplete understanding of the market mechanism. The coupling mechanism of electricity markets is based on increasing social welfare, being defined as the sum of the producer's surplus, the consumer's surplus and the revenues from the congestion. Thus, the market with the lower price exports electricity to the market with the higher price. The paper presents several numerical examples for understanding the coupling mechanism and the effects and particularities of the coupled functioning of the electricity markets. Also, the impact of increasing the share of renewable energy sources and support schemes on the negative prices recorded in the coupled electricity markets is analysed.

articleTitle: Whales Optimization Algorithm Based Enhanced Power Controller for an Autonomous Microgrid System
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This This paper proposes a study of optimal power controller based on Whales Optimization Algorithm (WOA) for PI controller tuning in an autonomous microgrid system (MGS). The MGS is based on multiple distributed generation (DG) connected with 120 kV power grid. The proposed controller with four different configurations i.e. controller without optimization, PSO, GWO, and WOA tuned controller will be validated to control and enhance the flow of active and reactive power between MGS and power grid grid-connected mode and during load variation. The simulation results show that MGS is supplying optimal power to utility grid also maintaining sinusoidal voltage and current supply with minimum THD levels. Further, results show that the WOA based controller optimizes the control parameters achieves the 38.46% and 75% better results in terms of active and reactive regulation and sharing, respectively. For modelling of proposed system and applying of optimization techniques, Matlab/Simulink and m/file have been used respectively. The proposed controller performs intelligently while sharing the load power between MGS and utility system.

articleTitle: Comparative Study a Two Adaptive Observers of Speed and Rotor Flux of the Induction Motor
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this article, a comparative study is being carried out between the extended Gopinath observer (EGO) versus the assembly consisting of the MRAS speed observer and the reduced order Gopinath observer, used in estimating dq components of the rotor flux phasor. Both observers are designed for sensorless vector control systems of the induction motors. Comparative analysis is performed by simulation using the Matlab-Simulink programming environment.

articleTitle: Short-Term Generation Forecasting Against the High Penetration of the Wind Energy
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The current renewable energy sources penetration increase requires adequate planning for the safe and reliable system operation, due to this energy to be an intermittent source. Considering that, this study aims to propose a modeling structure and simulation in the short-term horizon, applied to forecasting generation capacity from wind farms located in the southern region of Brazil. In view of the stochastic characteristics of wind energy forecasting were generated multi-scenarios by the Monte Carlo (MC) method. Besides, wind generation forecasting was modeled by a structure of Multilayer Perceptron Artificial Neural Networks (MLP NNs) due to its learning capacity of complex non-linear relations between input and output variables from a database. Taking into account that from a detailed planning begins the process of expansion the new enterprises electric power generating, this study brings an interesting tool for to predict the availability of renewable energy generation, like wind source.

articleTitle: Statistical analysis on wind variability impact on environment
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This document addressed a Romanian case for windfarm power output. A Matlab program was constructed, in order to assess the best goodness-of-fit (displacement of speed values from theoretical curves) for the deterministic wind speed. Subsequently, an interface was created, using Labview environment, in order to assess the electric power generation with respect to the instantaneous wind speed values. In the last part, a tool was designed in order to properly assess the CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>reduction with respect to traditional combustion power-plants.

articleTitle: Three Winding Transformers for Smart Power Substations
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Three-winding transformer model is widely utilized in High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) system or railway power supply system. Coupled with a diode rectifier, the application of three winding transformers for power distribution is now increasing because of increased demand for reliable and available electrical supply. This paper analyzes the application of a three-winding transformer as a primary power distribution system instead of a standard two-winding transformer. Moreover, we present a fast calculation of short circuit current.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of an Axial-Flux Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine for Railway Traction Application
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: It is well known that the synchronous machine with permanent magnets is one of the most efficient electric machines due to the lack of stator magnetization current and small losses in the rotor magnetic circuit. Besides these advantages, having a large number of poles and a large inner diameter of the rotor, the synchronous axial flux machine offers a compact integration in a direct drive propulsion system. This paper presents the 3D design and parametric optimization with finite element analysis of a three-phase permanent magnet axial-flux synchronous machine for railway traction to validate the performance indicators requested by the application.

Author Keywords: axial flux permanent magnet synchronous machine

articleTitle: Aspects Regarding the Electromagnetic Pattern for the Operating Mechanism of a Medium Voltage Circuit Breaker
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper presents a possibility to determine the electromagnetic pattern for the reinforcement electromotor, for the opening and closing electromagnets of the operating mechanism for a medium voltage circuit breaker using an electromagnetic field transducer.

articleTitle: Digitalization of Resource Consumption on the Basis of Innovative Devices of Demand Side Management in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The research is aimed at the development of digital models of managing Machine-to-Machine interaction in the system of Smart Grid on the basis of a new generation of devices of Demand Side Management NORMEL™<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">®©</sup>.

articleTitle: Aspects Regarding Contact Resistance Measurement
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The presence of an electrical contact on a current path always highlights an additional electrical resistance, called contact resistance R<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">c</sub>. The paper shows a method of measuring the contact resistance with the help of an equipment dedicated to this purpose. An experimental investigation of the contact resistance is presented on two switching equipment which have different types of contacts, at different values of the test current, related to their nominal current and at two thermal states (cold and warm).

articleTitle: Study on Illuminance Class Selection in Street Lighting Design
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents a technical study regarding Lighting Class Parameters and the way of selecting the carriageway lighting class in street lighting design around the world. The countries for which the study was made are: Romania, England, U.S.A. and Denmark. The study consists in Dialux calculation for each lighting class solution, as well as a comparison of the way of selecting the lighting classes. One conclusion of the paper is that, among the studied countries, the lighting classes with the highest consumption and the most restrictive norm when selecting the lighting class for each roads are in Romania, which actually gives the maximum W/km of road almost all the time.

articleTitle: Impact in the power system following the replacement of HVAC with HVDC lines in Dobrogea area
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Renewables have progressed at an unprecedented pace over the past decade and have consistently surpassed expectations, with new records being set each year and an increasing number of countries committing to their respective energy transitions. Much of the advancement has been achieved thanks to effective policies and planning, coupled with ambitious targets. The non-programmable nature of wind power plants leads to several challenging situations for the responsible system operator in the transmission grid and also in the distribution grid. In order to accommodate the installed power which is expected to appear in Dobrogea area, a number of investments have been proposed. The investments consist mainly in new AC lines. This paper analyses the impact in power system by replacing one of the planned AC line for power evacuation from Dobrogea area with a DC line.

articleTitle: Utilizing Short-Term Load Forecasts in the Assessment of Demand Response Programs
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The present paper proposes an integrated Demand Response (DR) methodology for eligible consumers in day-ahead markets. The test case refers to a high voltage industrial consumer of the Greek energy system. The first stage of the methodology involves a load profiling process to derive the typical load patterns of the consumers. Based on the shapes of the load profiles, a dedicated DR measure is designed for the purpose of manifesting a specific load modification target. The DR measure is supported with a Short-Term Load Forecasting (STLF) routine in day-ahead basis. In the paper, load predictions are treated as a tool that can provide information about the potential of the DR measures. Based on the forecasts, the DR are designed, implemented and evaluated.

articleTitle: Reliability of protection schemes used for multi-terminal transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Transelectrica's substations (Romanian Transmission and System Operator) are facing with various retrofit projects throughout the entire power system. Consequently, the initial network topology is changing during the retrofit process and different configurations of the network are adopted to maintain the stability and security of the power system. Multi-terminal transmission lines are often used in this situation. In this article is presented a protection scheme of a multi-terminal transmission line from Romanian power system. The security and selectivity criteria are assured with a grading plan of the protection functions. For a proper coordination of the protected zones, short circuit currents computation is realized in a modeling platform in which the entire 400/220/110 kV transmission and distributions network of the Romanian power system is designed. The protection system of the studied network area must detect and remove the unwanted condition within the fault clearing time. Taking into account what is mentioned above, a hybrid teleprotection scheme realized through a digital communication is proposed in order to improve functionality of multi-terminal transmission lines.

articleTitle: Reliability and Continuity Indicators Estimation in System of Electrical Power Supply to the Consumer
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Continuity indicators and that characterizing power quality are statistical parameters that describe, globally or locally, the state of operation of both, electrical power supply system and consumer equipment, as well as those belonging to consumers. Nowadays at the international level is not a unitary way of defining indicators, which quantify reliability of the electric power supply for consumers and to point the connection between the reliability indicators and the continuity of the electrical power supply indicators. The analysis of such indicators makes it possible to determine the quantity and quality of the necessary information and, on that basis, to adopt the measures as well as to reduce the economic consequences to a level of safety that can be accepted by the consumer and possible to be carried out by the operator of the electricity distribution. In this paper, an analysis of the reliability and continuity indicators are presented, and through the case study in a residential area, the link between the reliability of the electrical installation and the power quality through the quality of the service are established by analyzing SAIDI and SAIFI indicators. The results of case study support the factors involved in the choice of the optimal solution in such a way that the key performance indicators of the electricity network to be improved.

Author Keywords: quality of the electrical power supply

articleTitle: Influence of Multi-Pulse Rectifier on Power Quality in an Industrial Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The power quality in industry is actually of a greater importance due to the presence of sensitive loads like computers, protection relays, measurement and other electronic devices operated near the high-power nonlinear loads. One of the most important aspects of this quality is related to the harmonic distortion of voltage and current waves with the well-known negative consequences on the industrial power system components and its operating efficiency. This paper analyses the effects on the quality of electrical energy of the multipulse rectifiers used to supply some electrical high-power drives as main components of the production process, involved in the driving of the rolls of the scraper from a hot strip mill. The measurement results show clearly the advantage of the presence of the 6-pulse and 12-pulse rectifiers during the fast transient conditions of slab lamination.

articleTitle: EMC Study for Different Types of Lamps with the same Luminous Flux
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This article presents an electromagnetic study of conducted and radiated disturbances produced by the lamps. The analysis was performed on four types of lamps, the most common lamps: incandescent, halogen, compact fluorescent (CFL) and light-emitting-diode (LED), with the same luminous flux to determinate the conducted emissions and to determinate the radiated emissions. The experimental results and comments related to the limits for each type of lamp, especially the determination of conducted and radiated disturbances according to EN 55015 Standard, are also presented.

articleTitle: Method of Parameters Determination for Multi-Winding Transformer Equivalent Circuit in the Form of Multi-Beam Star
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: A technique is known for elaboration of equivalent schemes for transformers with two or three windings in the form of two or three beam stars (without electromagnetic coupling between the beam elements). Schemes usually contain the magnetization branch, connected to a common point. For the case of transformer with the number of windings four or more, the number of pair short-circuit impedances (which basically determined the main properties of transformer) is bigger than the number of beams of the corresponding star. This makes it impossible to obtain a sufficiently correct equivalent scheme in the form of a multi-beam star without electromagnetic coupling between the elements of the beams. An equivalent circuit in the form of complete polygon is also used; the number of polygon vertices is equal to the number of transformer windings. Also are used tree-like equivalent schemes that are approximate by nature. Besides, equivalent schemes of chain type are known, which have mutual electromagnetic coupling between the elements. However, for them the arrangement of the elements of the replacement circuit depends on the mutual arrangement of the transformer windings in the magnetic core window. In all these cases the problem arises of choosing the location of the magnetization branch connection point. In addition, these schemes (with the exception of the complete polygon scheme) are not universal, and the methods for determining their parameters are complex. In this paper, we propose a technique for determining the elements of the equivalent circuit for the replacement of a multi-winding transformer in the form of multi-beam star with mutual electromagnetic coupling between the elements of the beams with one magnetization branch. The basis for it is a formula, that connects the pair short-circuit impedance of the two windings with their full own and mutual impedances. Using the matrix pseudo-inversion procedure, a technique was developed for finding the own and mutual impedances, constituting the star's beams. This scheme is universal and did not depend on the specific mutual arrangement of the windings. Besides, it is possible to determine the parameters of the proposed multi-beam equivalent circuit in exact accordance with the values of the pair short-circuit impedances of the transformer. It is a logical continuation of the conventional equivalent scheme of three-winding transformer. In addition, the proposed algorithm ensures the positive values of the own inductive reactance of the beams (windings).

articleTitle: Economic Analysis of a Microgrid Considering Energy Markets
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper will be determined what is the optimal supply source for the loads of a microgrid in order that the total generation cost to be minimum. The power can be supplied from the power grid or from the microgrid generating units. The microgrid comprises seven generating units (renewable energy sources), loads and an energy management system based on a controller. An optimization will be performed to determine which units will supply power, so that the cost of the power supplied by the microgrid generating units to be minimum. After obtaining the optimization results, the total cost of the power supplied from the renewable energy sources will be compared with the cost of the power supplied from the grid. The cost of the power supplied from the grid is based on prices from two energy markets: the bilateral contracts energy market and the day-ahead energy market.

articleTitle: Analysis of V-trough reflector's geometry influence on Low Concentration Photovoltaic Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The solar radiation concentration technique can be used in order to increase the output of a photovoltaic system. The V-trough shape reflectors represent the most common solution for developing a low concentration system which can ensure a significant reduction of the cost per kilowatt-hour in the photovoltaic installations. In this sense, this paper aims to analytically investigate the influence of the V-trough reflectors length and the trough angle on the system's geometric and optical concentration ratios, as these parameters are key points when searching for an optimum design of the concentrator system.

articleTitle: Electric Locomotive Laboratory Test Bench for Research and Educational Purposes
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The article presents a laboratory test bench for an electric locomotive used for the research and educational purposes. The electric locomotive is on four axles, driven by four D.C. motors and supplied from a laboratory catenary on a truck of 6 meters. The laboratory test bench is realized as similar as possible to a real electric locomotive considering the supply system, the power collections system, the mechanical and electrical structure. A LabVIEW interface is used to control the locomotive from a computer.

articleTitle: Development of an automated system to optimize greenhouse resource consumption
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The rhythm of rising food prices due to unjustified consumption of resources is a fairly pronounced problem and a technological optimization of greenhouses in which they are cultivated is necessary. The proposed automation system aims both to reduce production costs due to the efficiency of water consumption and the elimination of the human factor in certain maintenance and care works as well as the improvement of plant growth factors. Simulation of the system automation consists in the practical execution of a miniature greenhouse system with a scale of 1:10, controlled by a development board equipped with Arduino, temperature, humidity and light intensity measuring elements, modules for interfacing the microcontroller with the elements respectively the sprinkler water pump, the ventilation fan and the motors for opening and closing the ventilation hatch. The automation system can be applied and adapted to an authentic agricultural greenhouse irrespective of its dimensions, but taking into account the required power of the electrical machines.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Evaluation of HV Power Supplies for Non-Thermal Plasma Generation
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Non-thermal plasma (NTP) technologies play an important role in different applications such air and water pollutants treatment or biological applications. The energy efficiency of the NTP reactors strongly depends on the type of the power supplies used to generate the electrical discharges. This study presents the evaluation of the energy efficiency for two different High Voltage power supplies (HVP): first is 9 kV, 50 Hz high voltage AC transformer and the second one is a pulse HV supply with frequency and pulse width control. In order to compare the energy efficiency of the power supplies, the concentration of the hydrogen peroxide generated in DI water treated by non-thermal plasma was measured.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic field radiation generated by pulsed non-thermal plasma discharge
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The benefits of non-thermal plasma have been proved effective in the agricultural field, medicine, and environmental control. The process used to obtain non-thermal plasma activated water uses a high voltage source and during plasma discharge is generated an electromagnetic radiation in the surrounding areas of the generator. The present paper assesses the radiated fields in the proximity of the non-thermal plasma reactors, during plasma activated water production, in order to identity their intensity for evaluating the impacts on the electronics or human operators in the near field. The electromagnetic fields are induced by electrical surface discharges and their intensity depends on the distance from the discharge point.

articleTitle: Calculation of Electromagnetic Field Produced by Mixed Overhead Power Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The main goal of this paper is the investigation of the electromagnetic field produced by mixed overhead power lines, containing two three-phase electric systems on different voltage levels; middle-voltage system, for the distribution purpose and the low-voltage level, for the supply of consumers. In this paper electric and magnetic field produced by maximal load of two symmetrical systems were explored. The calculation was performed for the situation when only MV system is in function and the case when both systems are operational. Electric and magnetic field are calculated separately, applying COMSOL Multiphysics computer program package, based on Finite Element Method. As expected, electric field, produced by a MV system is dominant and the contribution of LV system is neglizible. On the other hand, since the phase currents in the both systems can be of the same order, magnetic field of both systems must be taking into account. Moreover, with the different phase arrangement it can be achieved the minimal values of magnetic field in vicinity of the system conductors, which is crucial for the environment protection. The investigated model was the real system, applied in Serbia. The results of the calculations are presented graphically, by the diagrams of electric field strength vector spatial distribution in vicinity of the system, as well as the diagrams of magnetic flux density vector spatial distribution.

articleTitle: Automatic control systems in oil processing industry
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Development of automatic control systems in the oil processing industry and other industries, remains one of the major challenges nowadays. During this study we are going to analyze a project, where the control of the systems is carried out by pneumatic power system. A pneumatic system uses compressed air to transmit and control energy. Compressed air is produced by compressor that converts mechanical energy from motors and engines into the potential energy of compressed air. Pneumatic control systems are used in various industries especially in sectors for driving of automatic machines, control devices for the control of: level, temperature, pressure, etc. Based on the existing system we will propose a modern automatic control system, where process control will be done by electrical signal. Our analysis will be focused on the comparison of the existing model with the proposed models in some aspects to achieve a new level of: accuracy, speed of action, complexity, noise, quality of production and energy consumption. The universal nature of the approaches of proposed methodology makes it possible to use the template design of the automated control systems in other industries as well.

articleTitle: Implementation of an App for Android Mobile Devices Designed for Electromagnetic Field Problems Solving
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper describes the design and implementation of a software application, an app created for mobile devices with Android operating system, as a support tool for students from the Electrical Engineering bachelor level study programs to understand the solving methods of several Electromagnetic Field Theory problems. The implemented app entitled MAGELFAPP can be used also in Electromagnetic Field Numerical Modeling problem solving where numerical modeling programs (such as Ansoft Maxwell) offer also the possibility to validate the results.

articleTitle: Water Exposure and Thermal Aging Effects on Dielectric Response of Liquid Silicone Rubber Insulators
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Water exposure and thermal aging effects on the dielectric response of LSR insulator samples were analyzed in this paper. The dielectric spectra of the real and imaginary permittivities, over a frequency range of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-2</sup>-10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> Hz and for temperatures from 30 to 70 °C, measured before any exposure, after one week immersion in deionized water and after one month thermal aging at 90 °C are presented and discussed in this paper.

articleTitle: Assessment of DFIG wind turbine overvoltage protection system for grid stability
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Power system stability with integrated wind energy is susceptible to power grid parameters variation, fault occurrence and recovery conditions. The present paper studies the susceptibility of the overvoltage and overcurrent protection system in the event of a short circuit fault in the grid and its influence on wind turbine DFIG response. Short circuit conditions in power systems must be cleared rapidly and the protection system in the wind turbine rotor will be triggered, and thus the rotor side converter disabled.

articleTitle: Temperature logger for Electrical Equipment's Thermal Stress Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper aims to present the importance of the electrical equipment's temperature monitoring by highlighting how its thermal stresses can indicate a malfunction of equipment. When defective electrical equipment or improper electric loading or damaged metallic or non-metallic components occur, they are usually due to abnormal temperature models. Also the paper presents the development and manufacturing of a temperature logger that can successfully monitor the thermal stress of electrical equipment in multiple independent points. In addition, the paper shows how the thermal stress of a busbar connection are monitored by the temperature logger. By the laboratory experiment is intended to exemplify how important is to have enough number of temperature monitoring points of the electrical equipment's constructive elements.

articleTitle: Lifetime Availability Analysis of High Voltage Circuit Breakers for Maintenance Optimization
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Different maintenance methods are used in industry. The classic preventive planned one is mainly replaced by the preventive opportune type. The second is based on state condition monitoring of different power systems components. Unfortunately it is expensive and only in few cases are technically and economically justified. This paper present a technique to evaluate the maintenance policy efficiency and, finally to rank the subsytems of high voltage circuit-breakers aiming to select what subsystem can be selected for state monitoring. A large database for 12 circuit-breakers was used and the information about failures and maintenance during 33 years was used for analysis.

articleTitle: Thermal simulation of a power transformer
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In the article we propose a method of thermally constructive optimization of a 110/20 kV power transformer by numerical simulation (by the finite element method) of the thermal field in the transformer. The thermal simulation was done in the Comsol module called Heat Transfer Module, based on the documentation in Catia V5, and the experimental validation was done by thermography.

articleTitle: Considerations about Fault Loop Impedance Measurement in TN Low-Voltage Network
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Loop testing is one of the most difficult measurement performed, day to day, by the electrical technicians. Choosing the tests methods, correlation with instrument accuracy and understanding the external factors that influence the measured result are challenges that the electricians have to deal with. This paper presents some considerations about the equivalent fault-loop circuits, in terms of proximity to the distribution transformer and particularly configurations, TN-S or TN-C networks. We analyzed the measured parameters and successive tests to be done, possible sources of errors and in the final stage the conclusion regarding the network security degree.

articleTitle: The Effect of Corrosion on Electrical Contacts
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In electrical fuses problems due to high electrical currents and weakened electrical contacts can arise, but these problems are invisible to the human eye. Thermo graphing can verify the state of the fuses, in different types of charging conditions, respectively other side problems, which can damage the quality of the exterior environment. This limitation comes from the large difference between the temperature of the electrical contact points which are overheated and the temperature of the exterior surfaces. The goal of the article is to demonstrate the influence of the aging and corrosion phenomenon on the electrical circuits. With help of simulations carried out by numerical modelling programs and obtained results a complex voltage, current and temperature monitoring system using a microcontroller has been developed.

articleTitle: Numerical Modeling and Parametric Analysis of Induction Plates
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Starting from an induction plate often encountered in kitchen households, different geometries for this device will be numerically modeled in order to analyze their functionality, ohmic losses, magnetic induction and current density. Also, the effects of parameter variation will be highlighted. The model was analyzed in 2D and also in 3D. The varied parameters were number of turns, diameter of the conductor from which the turns are constructed, the shape of the conductor and the material from which the recipient where the food is heated is made of. The novelty of this study is the ohmic losses approach and the software used for the simulation. The representations can be also used in educational purposes.

articleTitle: Design Analysis of a Toroidal Transformer for Traction Application
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper approaches the electromagnetic design and finite-element analysis of two types of transformers to be used in electric traction applications. A comparison is made between a single phase toroidal transformer and a classical construction type transformer, with columns. The benefits for such an application of the toroidal transformer topology over the classic transformers are highlighted by the finite element method analysis results.

articleTitle: Local Monitoring / Recording and Display Device for Power Electricity Meter, using IEC 62056–21 Local AMR application device, hardware solution, for DLMS-COSEM based Power Meters
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper describes a microcontroller-based device that provides real time locally data display and record, for several electrical parameters, acquired from a smart power and energy meter device. The aim of this device is to provide directly access to momentary power consumption information, graphically displayed as a process diagram on a monitoring graphic panel, or remotely by using a computer or mobile devices. Thereby, the customer can more easily manage his power consumption manner. The device can be used as an AMR (Automatic Meter Reading) gateway, by changing the firmware suitable made for another communication standard (e.g. IEC 62056-47, 7-x, 9-x). For acquiring information, the presented solution uses serial interface, directly connected to the energy meter, and a communication protocol described in IEC 62056-21 standard. Parameters are sorted and stored on an internal memory card and displayed, as numbers and time diagram on a graphic panel, but can be remotely accessed, by using a pair of Client-Server applications. The device was designed to be connected in a home, or residential, TCP/IP and Ethernet based network, which makes it very useful as an interface with other communication technologies.

articleTitle: Analysis of the wholesale energy market price in Romania and its impact on the end customer
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The Romanian energy market is a specific one through the lack of predictability on medium and long term. As any other free market, the price on retail and wholesale markets is based on supply and demand. However, the price even for this calendar year varies for the end customer based on the time of purchase, how the price is warranted and the consumption structure. Investors and businesses for which the energy costs are significant have a real problem in Romania to budget these costs every year. This paper aims by analyzing a relevant wholesale market to statistically identify the right moment for these end customers to purchase the energy and under what circumstances the purchase price is guaranted.

Market Clearing Price (Preţul de Închidere a Pieţei - PIP) [1]
