articleTitle: Software Redundancy Implementation Strategy in Reconfigurable Hardware Framework
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In recent years reconfigurable hardware technology (RHT) has emerged as one of the most challenging implementation paradigm of modern digital systems. In comparison with previously used other technologies RHT exhibits a few of remarkable advantages in terms of processing speed, flexibility, implementation costs, or energy consumption. The most representative RHT-based component is the FPGA (Field Programmable Gate Array) processor. This paper focuses on the main idea that FPGA-based digital system implementations may provide other additional facilities like the above mentioned ones. In particular, there it is emphasized that the RHT is also well fitted for software redundancy strategies implementation. In order to evidence this facility a given control algorithm has been implemented in two different RH-based software technologies that are supported on the same FPGA-based digital system. One version is linked to the VHDL (Very high speed IC's Hardware Description Language) software framework, the second one to the embedded SDK (Software Development Kit) firmware support. The result of this implementation is a high reliability control application that embeds a versatile software redundancy solution. The implemented framework may serve as a useful support and guidance for a wide range of demanding industrial applications that require high safety and reliability during their operation.

articleTitle: Contactless excitation system with rotary transformer for hydro-generators
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents a new application of contactless electrical power transmission, namely the realization of contact-less excitation systems for hydroelectric power plants. The main excitation systems used in hydro-generators construction are presented, as well as the new solution proposed in this paper. The proposed contactless excitation system for hydro-generators transmits the required electrical energy to the hydro-generator's excitation coil, placed in the rotor, through a medium-frequency rotary transformer, and includes frequency converters on both the primary and the secondary side of the transformer placed on the hydro-generator rotor. In this way, both the advantage of fast static excitation systems (without the high time constants rotating electric machines) and easy maintenance provided by brushless excitation systems is maintained. The design methodology for these non-contact excitation systems is presented, as well as an application for a 75 MW hydro-generator, in operation in Romania.

articleTitle: Research on the Realization of a Electromechanical Pressure Micropump Used in Electrical Equipment
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper aims to determine the characteristics of Nitinol smart materials with memory of the shape and to determine their behavior on repeated cycles of use. The system consists of a protrusion of a electromechanical pressure micro-pump made on the basis of current-controlled Nitinol arc elements, with the purpose of regulating the pressure inside a fluid enclosure. In the paper there will be presented characteristics concretized in the pressure variation inside the enclosure with the pressure gauge connected at the opposite end of the container, both positive pressure and negative pressure depending on the group of springs in Nitinol.

articleTitle: Analysis of the necessity of installing flexible AC transmission devices in the National Power System in the context of increase power in the Dobrogea area
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: On the premise of developing sources of renewable energy, with a focus on the wind power plants in Dobrogea area, the current paper outlines a projected scenario of an electric power increase in the aforementioned area in line with grid connection contracts and the impact of a potential power growth might bear on the electric grid of transportation. Hereby shall be analysed the utility of having installed flexible alternating current transmission system - FACTS inside the National Power System so as to adjust the voltages in the grid's nodes susceptible to problems. The equipment to be utilised is the static synchronous compensator - STATCOM. The analysis is conducted on the perspective grid for 2022, within which 400 kV OHL Cernavodă - Stâlpu is assumed, for which financing from the European Commission has been secured.

articleTitle: Analysis of coexistence conditions between an overhead electricity lines and a dwelling house
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: According to the General Urbanism Regulations, in areas exposed to technological risks, as well as in areas of service and protection of power supply systems, it is forbidden. In practice, the technical norms for the construction of overhead electrical lines with a voltage greater than 1000 V and the Technical Norm for the delimitation of protection and safety areas related to energy capacities allow for the placement of buildings including in the field of protection and safety from the energy capacities subject to the coexistence standardized conditions. Establishing coexistence conditions involves a complex analysis, it is necessary to develop a coexistence study. The coexistence study is the technical and economic documentation in which the mechanical and/or electrical implications of the electrical network are determined on the basis of calculations, measurements, observations, etc., the location of other installations or networks on the elements of the corridor or its protection and/safety and, where appropriate, the work required to meet the conditions of coexistence provided for by the rules and the costs of such works.

articleTitle: Flexible System for Practical Hands-On Power Electronics Teaching
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper presents a dedicated teaching platform focused primarily on teaching the basics of power electronics in Electrical Engineering domain. The proposed system is dedicated to practical implementation, measurements and analysis of the main power converters topologies used in different energy conversion applications.

articleTitle: Simulation of a Boost Converter for the Automotive Industry
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper describes an analyze and a simulation comparison between 2 types of coils for a DC-DC boost converter. The analysis of the circuit is realized with two different types of software which have the same method of compilation. The presented study was used as a reference point for the integrated circuit (IC), ISL “78227”, circuit that has been used in the series production for automotive industry projects, especially as a boost converter driver. The DC-DC boost converter was designed to rise up the voltage from Vin=9V up to Vout_1=50V and Vout_2=55V. During the simulation, the main focus stayed on the circuit design within two simulation software and also on the component parametrization in according with the components that were taken in consideration within the project requirements. Nevertheless, the paper presents the results that were obtain after the simulation and also shown both variants of the output voltage in according with the project requirements. The work contains also a comparison between the functionality and the malfunction of the system for the 2-phase usage of the boost converter.

articleTitle: Single-phase Auto-Reclose Automation in medium voltage network
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper presents the theoretical concepts and studies the technical impact of the implementation of single-phase reclose automation on the medium voltage overhead lines belonging to networks grounded using Peterson coil or resistor.

articleTitle: Power Analysis Tools Developed in the LabVIEW Programming Environment
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The current paper presents some basic tools developed in the LabVIEW environment. It is focused on the mathematical formulation and the implementation of the equation. It will show a simple solution developed by the authors for some of the most necessary parameters used in the Power analysis literature, like: determining the fundamental frequency of a signal, linear filtration using DFT, computation of the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), determining the initial phase of an acquired signal or a method for phase shifting.

articleTitle: Prosumers optimally adapted to local load. Rationale and benefits for the grid
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Prosumers are entities with a key role in the new smart grid paradigm, having enabled two ways active power exchange. The usual approach is to send excess energy to the main grid, with a cost of unpredictability of the reverse power flow. In order to achieve a high penetration of renewables in the distribution grid, with added contribution from prosumers, traditional grids need to be operated in states corresponding to active grids for which they have not been designed. Recently deployed solutions allow advanced prosumers to benefit from advancements in both storage and renewables technologies, changing the behavior of prosumers into controlled unidirectional power exchange (no-back generation), which translates into consumer-only behavior from the grid side. With this no-back generation paradigm, in this paper a number of comprehensive scenarios have been simulated and analyzed on a daily basis, based on real local production and consumption profiles and using key performance indexes. The paper shows the benefits of operating and customers with prosumers potential, which can bring substantial openings for a high renewables penetration agenda to address climate change related issues.

articleTitle: Requirements of a real time monitoring and analysis system of power losses in electrical transmission and distribution systems
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In the process of power supply to final consumers, an important amount of energy is lost in the transmission and distribution systems due to technological and non-technological losses. These power losses are often referred to as “line losses”, even if line losses represent only one type of power loss that occurs during the process of transmission and distribution of electricity. Each component of the power transmission and distribution system contributes to losses, so that a reduction in loss at the final consumer will be felt significantly at the generation level. Technical losses represent an economic loss with environmental effects at national level, and its optimization should be performed from an overall national's perspective, regardless of the institutional organization of the sector and ownership of operating electricity utilities [1]. EU Energy Efficiency Directive 27/CE/2012 states for an important obligation for utility companies to improve energy efficiency in delivering services to their customers. The Directive establishes a common framework of measures to promote energy efficiency within the Union in order to ensure the achievement of the 20% target for energy efficiency by 2020 and to pave the way for the future growth of energy efficiency beyond that date [2]. The volume of energy losses in the power transmission and distribution systems is important, as it is generally up to 3-13%. The volume of power losses in Romanian power transmission and distribution systems is important, the level being of about double to the average in Europe. The current paper presents the research results of the authors regarding the real time monitoring and analysis systems for power losses, in electrical transmission and distribution systems.

articleTitle: Challenges of non-formal methods in electrical engineering education
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper proposes a set of exercises in order to train transversal and professional competencies within the electrical engineering field, which activates both aptitudes and attitudes.

articleTitle: Complex Power Quality Analysis of Electric Waveforms Affected by Noise
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper is concerned with a thorough study relative to some of the most representative power quality indices characterizing electric waveforms affected by white noise. 6 sets of experimental data were acquired from a key point of the electrical network of a large power group. An original denoising technique was conceived in order to evaluate the power of noise for the analyzed three-phase systems components and to perform denoising. Four techniques were used in order to decompose the waveforms before and after denoising: FFT, Discrete Wavelet Transform, Wavelet Packet Transform and Stationary Wavelet Transform. A comparative study "polluted versus denoised” was performed and conclusions were drawn. Whilst FFT proved a sort of "immunity” to noise, all wavelet techniques were found to be more or less sensitive to its presence. The study of errors corresponding to each level from the wavelet decomposition trees allowed for the determination of the lowest level for which the noise has a negligible influence.

articleTitle: Monitoring the Cost of Energy for Powering the Railway Electric Traction System
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper deals with the analysis of the particularities of the electric power supply of the railway electric transport systems and the methodology for monitoring and evaluation of the electricity costs in order to develop efficient methods for reducing the losses and, implicitly, reducing the price of energy. The cost methodology for this consumer is analysed, on the basis of which an algorithm is developed and a software module is proposed to monitor the cost of energy needed to power the electric traction system. With the developed methodology and module, the cost of active and reactive energy is calculated and displayed. The results show that the contribution of reactive energy is significant in the total energy cost, which justifies the introduction of the power factor compensation systems, and the active filters to reduce the impact of the harmonics in the supply system.

articleTitle: New Modalities in Performing the “abc-$\alpha\beta$” and “$\alpha\beta$-abc” Coordinates Conversion using Hilbert Transform
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper presents new modalities to transform the relations from the “abc” coordinates to the “ αβ” coordinates and vice versa using the Hilbert transform. The new analysis of the unbalanced three-phase system is achieved by symmetrical components method. The method is based on the properties of the Hilbert transform. At the beginning, relations are developed for calculating the symmetrical components in “abc” natural coordinates of a three-phase system. In the end, similar relationships in “ αβ” coordinates are developed. There are also presented the conversion relations between different quantities expressed in both coordinate systems. The analysis is done for the general case of an unbalanced, non-sinusoidal, distorted three-phase system. Symmetrical components will be implicitly determined for each group of harmonics of the same frequency. The main conclusion is that the Hilbert transform based method represents an important analytical and computational tool regarding the unbalanced three-phase systems.

articleTitle: eXtended Finite Element Method Connected with Multi-objective Optimization Algorithm Used in 3D Electromagnetic Problems
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper describes a way to interconnect the independent mesh mode, eXtended Finite Element Method (XFEM), with multi-objective optimization mode based for the improvement process on the genetic evolution algorithms Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). XFEM is an approximation method and is mostly used in dealing with problems characterized by deformations, cracks, discontinuities, complex geometries and it doesn't require that the mesh must conform to the geometrical boundaries. NSGA-II is an evolutionary multi-objective optimization algorithm used on a large scale to generate solutions in different domains. The solution returned is on the form of the Pareto Front. This approach to couple XFEM method with NSGA-II optimization algorithm is of the interest from the perspective of using XFEM method which has the advantage of not being necessary to remesh the model at each step of the optimization process while the NSGA-II Algorithm is an iterative process who succeeds to generate optimal solutions for the studied objective functions. This developed system can be used in various three-dimensional (3D) optimization problems while maintaining the advantages of the XFEM method and meanwhile optimizing the model through the robust process used by the NSGA-II algorithm.

articleTitle: Wind farms behaviour at power grid voltage dips
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Wind power plants have technical and operating characteristics that significantly differ from other types of power plants, such as the power available at each moment and wind power installed, the technical performance of wind farms in the event of system disturbances, the volatility and the unpredictability of wind power production. Therefore, it is necessary to analyze the specific problems raised by the installation of wind farms and identify the necessary measures to solve them before connecting a significant volume of wind power energy. One of the main requirements to be met by wind farms is fault ride through. The present paper aims to study the impact of the grid faults on the wind turbines at the connection point and on their generators and is presented as a teaching tool that can be useful for students in renewable power system applications.

articleTitle: Comparative WLAN exposure analysis: weighted channel power method versus CCDF method
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper investigates the accuracy of assessing exposure to radiation emitted by sources specific to the IEEE 802.11n communication standard by two methods. The first one is based on weighing of the maximum power channel measured in the frequency domain and the second one uses the complementary cumulative distribution function (CCDF) acquisition mode of a real-time spectrum analyzer. It has been demonstrated that the CCDF method is much proper to be applied in the case of the quasi-stochastic signals such as WLAN's.

articleTitle: EOG based Controll of a Graphical Interface System for Assisting Paraplegic Patients
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper presents a LabVIEW implementation of an algorithm for processing the EOG signal, that detects the both vertical and horizontal voluntary movements of the eye and the eye blinks. Furthermore, based on the processed EOG signal, a graphical interface is controlled, for helping paraplegic persons to communicate and interact with those around them.

Author Keywords: eye movement and eye blinking detection

articleTitle: Case study of Transient Regimes in Distribution Network With Distributed Generators
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper it was analyzed the influence of a distributed renewable sources of medium voltage power network of the various fault regimes. The real electrical network considered is complex and, depending on the operating scheme, it can contain up to four renewable sources. This real three-phase electrical network was implemented in the “ATP - Alternative Transients Program” software for which the electrical parameters of the model have been transmitted by the power network operator's staffs. It is well-know that for the analysis of the transient regimes an important factor is the connected modes and parameters of the neutral grounding of the power network. For the studied 20 kV network, the neutral can operate with Petersen coil and also with low impedance resistor. Simulations have been made in the ATP model of the network in the event of the occurrence of various types of faults, near the 20kV bus-bars of the substation and at a further point in the grid, near one of the renewable sources.

articleTitle: Comparison of the Electromagnetic Performances of Rare Earth-less Outer Rotor Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents a comparison of two rare-earth less outer rotor electrical machines suitable for industrial applications like fans, conveyors etc. After few basic theoretical considerations on an induction machine and a variable reluctance synchronous machine, a study based on numerical analysis is performed for both machines. The most important electro-mechanical quantities of the analyzed structures are obtained from steady state and transient regime calculations. Conclusions regarding the performed study are presented in the final part of the paper.

articleTitle: Assessment of Photovoltaic Modules' Parameters Using the On-Site Measurements
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Among various renewable energy sources, the photovoltaic technology is considered the proper technology for distributed power generation. The performance of photovoltaic panels depends on their electrical characteristics on various environmental conditions. The objective of this paper is to use the one-diode model together with on-site measurements, in order to evaluate the current-voltage and power-voltage curves and effects of irradiance and temperature on the performance the photovoltaic panel.

articleTitle: Generating Waveforms for EMI Filters Testing
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In recent decades, the demand for energy produced from renewable sources has increased due to environmental problems and declining fuel classical sources: oil, coal and natural gas. One of the most commonly renewable energy used to connect to the grid are photovoltaic systems. This paper addresses specific problems regarding the design and simulation of EMI filters. Throughout this paper we have presented a method of simulating harmonics waveforms using CIGUI software.

articleTitle: Optimization of a Power Line Communications Network for Smart Metering System
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The main goal of the paper aims to investigate, develop and test experimentally a self optimal reconfigurable Power Line Communications Network (PLCN) that constitutes the power metering infrastructure of an electrical distribution grid. A solution based on optimization algorithm that offers the optimal configuration of the system on providing reliable field data acquisition related to the energy consumption in special requirements consumers is proposed and developed in the paper. Experimental results and discussions regarding the proposed optimization model are also presented along with conclusions and best practices recommendations that are also included.

articleTitle: Investigation of the possibilities of increasing the frequency converter efficiency based on the phase-shift transformer
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper provide the study of the frequency converter characteristics based on a phase-shift transformer (PSF) with a circular rotation of the phase, controlled by means of power electronics. The novelty of the research lies in the development of ways to improve the quality of power transmission in telecommunications when combining power systems with different frequencies. The selection and comparison of possible circuit options for the implementation of the device, as well as control strategies that meet the requirements for the quality of electricity on the receiving and transmitting power system bars, was carried out. The research results will contribute to the determination of feasibility and technical efficiency of the new types converters use for the integration of asynchronously operating power systems.

articleTitle: LabVIEW Program for Implementing Hilbert Spaces Algorithms in Power Systems Analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper aims to show the practical implementation of numeric calculus of the Hilbert spaces theory applied in the power analysis and compensation. While we wrote about equations and calculation methods, this paper is expressing the actual work done in LabVIEW programing environment. Numerical analysis programs have numerical computing tools for these sizes. Thus, the analysis of polyphase circuits can be done easily. Further analysis examples will be carried out using Hilbert spaces. LabVIEWapplications have been developed to implement the algorithms described in the theoretical part. The application is adaptable for any number voltage and current systems. The examples will be dedicated to penta-phase systems.

articleTitle: Case study on the protection of power stations against ligthning strokes
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper, a typical example of power substation has been proposed. Two approaches have been exposed and compared, the standard method and the electro-geometrical method. The example has been illustrated through a case-study aimed at revealing the importance of each method, with their specific protective zones and the choosing of the appropriate one.

articleTitle: Urban Energy Management, from concept to action and results
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In the paper, the author is briefly presenting the urban energy management concept, programs and specific actions, related to both technical and scientific research issues. Achieved results are then showed for several Romanian local communities, as case studies presented in the paper.

Author Keywords: demand response on blocks of buildings

articleTitle: Hardware and software solution for the electronic equipment in the process of extracting methane gas from the coal deposit
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Both in the exploitation of coal deposits and in the safety of the underground by its isolation from the surface, the presence of large amounts of methane gas is a source of danger to the safety of underground work, the dangers that arise with the increase in the depth of exploitation, increasing production capacity and mechanizing the extraction of coal through high-capacity exploitations, and closing work fronts. From the history of mining, it is known that methane explosions have been the source of numerous catastrophes in which human lives have been lost.

articleTitle: Variable High Frequency Power Inverter used in Wireless Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Power supply is the heart of a wireless power transfer system. A bigger power to transfer requires a bigger power supply and a bigger distance requires a higher frequency of the alternating current generated by power supply. Being able to vary the frequency of alternating current can improve efficiency of the transfer.

articleTitle: Solution for Reducing Technological Consumption in Low Voltage Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Improving energy efficiency is one of the priority elements of the energy strategy both in our country and in the world. Increasing energy efficiency has a major contribution to delivering food security, sustainability and competitiveness. In addition, increasing efficiency in electrical networks is done by developing and applying solutions that reduce electrical power losses. Considering that the share of household electricity consumption is growing worldwide, this paper presents a solution for reducing technological consumption in low voltage distribution network.

articleTitle: Substation Lightning Protection
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper makes an analysis of the variation of the protection area parameters provided by two identical lightning poles, that form the protective system against the direct lightning, of a 110kV high-voltage substation.

Author Keywords: minimum width of the protection area

articleTitle: Estimation of Line Zero Sequence Impedance using Real Field Fault Data for Fault Location Application
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper presents how the zero sequence parameters of the line can be estimated using the real field zero sequence quantities of voltage and currents from both ends of the line, after the occurrence of an unbalanced fault involving the ground. The new zero sequence parameters of the line calculated in this way are different that the ones implemented in the real relays. Furthermore, these new estimated line parameters are used to calculate again the fault locations from both ends of the line and the results show fairly improvements when they are compared with the results provided by the real relays.

articleTitle: Battery Energy Storage Applications: Two Case Studies
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The worldwide increasing energy consumption resulted in a demand for more load on existing electricity grid. The electricity grid is a complex system in which power supply and demand must be equal at any given moment. Constant adjustments to the supply are needed for predictable changes in demand, such as the daily patterns of human activity, as well as unexpected changes from equipment overloads and storms. Energy storage plays an important role in this balancing act and helps to create a more flexible and reliable grid system. In additional, most developed countries have adopted policies to reduce nuclear and fossil fuel consumption and to increase the renewabies energy plant as wind power, hydroelectric, solar thermal, solar thermo-electric and photovoltaic. To reduce the dependence of the renewable energy on the hour duration of the wind and sun it is important to develop and use the various technologies of energy storage. Among these, battery energy storage systems (BESS) are currently escalating and trending major growth in the world market. The paper mainly discuss different applications of BESS and exemplifies with two study cases.

articleTitle: Improving Performance Standards and Reducing Technical Loss By Mounting of Electrical Energy Storage Batteries Connected to 0,4kV-20kV Lines
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Reducing the cost of manufacturing batteries for electricity storage has led EU Electricity Distributors OD to investment programs in battery storage systems and the supply of electricity stored at daily peak load or in case of damage to the regional power supply consumers over limited time periods. Combined with the possibility of powering storage batteries in local photovoltaic or wind farms, the storage of electricity and the delivery to the energy system leads to the reduction of the Technological Consumption, the elimination of the interruptions in the power supply of the consumers and implicitly the development of a regional business for the Operators OD sale of electricity from renewable sources.

articleTitle: A Simplified Model for Approximating the Vias in the Thermo-Mechanical Simulation of Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Structures
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Finding a qualitative model to study the thermo-mechanical effects inside the Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor power Integrated Circuits (MOS power IC's) is needed even from the design stage of such devices. The high number of geometry details contained by these devices, especially at the level of the metallization system, rise difficulties in the Finite Element Method (FEM) analyze, thus some simplifications are needed. In this paper a simple method of geometry details reduction is proposed, in order to eliminate some geometrical details such as vias between two different metal layers. While the geometry details are simplified, the thermo-mechanical behavior is assessed on a simple Double-Diffused MOS (DMOS) substructure with an open source software (Code_Aster) based on FEM. In order to understand the influence of vias at the metallization level, temperature and strain distributions are compared for three different cases with vias, no-vias and equivalent materials properties block respectively. The no vias model approach capture with less computational effort and good accuracy the thermal induced metal deformation.

articleTitle: Energy Demand Curve Modeling with Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper, a neural algorithm based on Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture able to model the energy demand as a time sequence application and predict trends based on key identified factors that influence energy consumption is proposed.

articleTitle: High Frequency Analysis of Bandpass Filters
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The filters are widely used in high frequency applications. It is very important to use the proper filter for each type of application. For this reason, is a necessity analyzing the filter in order to find his parameters. The goal of this paper is the high frequency analysis of bandpass filters in order to extract the S parameters, to evaluate the filter behavior in a certain band of frequency, to represent the electric field intensity in different planes and the current density on the conductors from which the filter is constructed for different configurations. Different structures of bandpass filters will be analyzed in a wide range of frequency.

articleTitle: Interferences in High Voltage AC Power Line and Electric Railway Common Right-of-Way
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The paper studies the magnetic and electric field distribution around a Romanian high voltage overhead power line and an electrified railway traction system in order to highlight the induced voltages in nearby metallic structure. Numerical simulation and on-site measurements was carryout. Obtained numerical results are related to the appropriate regulations regarding the human exposure to electric and magnetic fields.

articleTitle: Transient Phenomena and Failures Analysis in Redundant Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In last decades a remarkable progress has been reached in the development of power electronic technologies. This achievement has been driven by major factors such as the successive apparition of high reliability gate-controlled power devices or improving cost-effectiveness of electronic commutation. In spite of all these achievements faults remains unavoidable in power electronic converters and their fault-tolerance represents a major design issue for researchers and developers. This paper presents a specially designed power converter topology that uses hardware redundancy strategy in order to achieve its high safety and fault-free operation. For this purpose an original mathematical model has been developed that is full suitable to model a wide range of faulty states in power converter modules. The proposed model has been validated through detailed computer simulations. The designed hardware redundant power converter architecture embeds two stand alone inverter modules interconnected into a parallel operation and switching topology. During the laboratory experiments this configuration has proved a high degree of reliability and fault-free operation. In order to evidence the complex switching events and occurred transient states a set of real-time waveform plots have been captured. Thorough analyses confirm that the proposed redundant converter topology is well suited for utilization in a wide range of applications that require high safety and reliable operation. Such solutions are specially recommended in critical industrial application where damages or material losses are impermissible at all.

articleTitle: Energy Management on Water Supply Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The quality of public water supply services is an indicator of living standards. Energy management based on professional energy studies can increase the energy efficiency of these energy-intensive services, implicitly at reducing costs, increasing the population's accessibility to them and also positively impacting the environment. The paper presents on the basis of the energy audit the comparative situation of the three options of equipping a water supply system.

articleTitle: The Analytical Method of Calculating the Transient Process in the Circuit's with Distributed and Concentrated Parameters
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In the paper is substantiates the methodology of calculation of the transitory process in the electrical circuit, which including of portions with distributed parameters and concentrated parameters. The purpose of this paper is to obtain and analyze the precise analytical solutions of the current and voltage wave propagation processes in the nonhomogeneous electrical circuits with the multiple reflections. The calculation of voltage and current in line and load is done using partial derivative equations. These equations are transformed into equations with the single variable by using of additional functions, which are Riemann invariants. The initial and limit conditions were formulated. The algorithm for calculating Riemann invariants has been proposed. These invariants are used to solve the Cauchy problem. Was the obtained of the general solution for calculating the current and voltage at the input and at the end of the line for different values of the active, inductive and capacitive components of the complex load. The solution elucidates the multiple reflections effect of the current and voltage waves in the examined circuit. Results of the calculation of the dynamic regime in the analyzed circuit are presented. The phenomenon of continuous energy accumulation in the inductance at the end of the line has been detected. This is possible in the wave propagation regime in the portion circuit with the distributed parameter's. This regime can be used to store energy in inductivitie with superconductivity. Analytical solutions can serve as standard solutions for verifying precision, for example, of the numerical solutions.

articleTitle: Comparative Determinations of Magnetic Induction in AC and DC Circuits
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The influence of the electromagnetic field on the human body, although still heavily studied, can have long-term negative effects. The static electromagnetic field is generated by a continuous current source and has a current flow characteristic conventionally set + from -. The variable electromagnetic field is produced by the alternating current and has the ability to change its direction over time with a frequency of 50 or 60 Hz. It is considered that the non-hazardous limit value for the magnetic field (according to Federal Office for Radiation Security in Germany) is 100 microT for 50 Hz and 83 microT for 60 Hz. For the electric field, the exposure limit value is 5kV/m. Electromagnetic fields are not attenuated by obstacles The consumption of electricity is accompanied by their prevalence. The paper aims to determine the values of the magnetic field around the conductors traveled by AC and DC and proposals for its mitigation.

articleTitle: An Efficient Approach for Flattening the Electricity Consumption Profile at Small and Medium Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Production scheduling represents a significant tool for reducing the cost of electricity bills, flattening the consumption profile, energy conservation, improving the energy efficiency and economic performance, and strengthening competitiveness at small and medium enterprises (SMEs). Considering these aspects, an efficient approach for flattening the electricity consumption profile based on the production scheduling at SMEs was proposed. The optimal solutions were obtained using combinational optimization. The approach was tested at an industrial consumer (a small enterprise in the automobile repair activity domain). The obtained results led at a decrease of peak values of the electricity consumption with 15.87%.

articleTitle: Considerations about Substation Grounding System Design
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This work analyses the parameters that influence the design of grounding system for substations. From these, the grid geometry is defined by some variables which influence drastically the touch and step voltages. The design procedure, based on Romanian standards, is briefly described and applied on an example. The values of above mentioned quantities are modified, the results being interpreted focusing both technical and economical perspectives. Finally a recommended design procedure, to achieve a technical and economical optimum is presented.

articleTitle: A Numerical Analysis of the Harmonic Impedance in a Medium Voltage AC Network
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Under the current conditions of the increasing harmonic pollution of three-phase distribution networks, the correct determination of the harmonic impedance of a network in a section or in a consumer bus becomes more and more important. This is due to the importance of harmonic impedance used as a tool of analysis and basing of the solutions required to increase the network performance, including the power quality delivered to consumers. The article uses the results of the numerical analysis applied in a case study performed for a medium voltage distribution network, like a real one, in order to demonstrate that the underground electrical lines of relatively long lengths significantly influence the harmonic modelling of the network and the correctness of the harmonic impedance values. In addition, the model of such a line must consider the distributed equivalent parameters, which becomes an imperative requirement when seeking to obtain the correct values for the equivalent harmonic impedance of the network.

articleTitle: Determining the Response of a Mechanical Shock Transducer Based on a Hall Effect Sensor
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents aspects regarding the response of a mechanical shock transducer that contains a Hall effect sensor as detecting element. An algorithm was developed in order to predict and analyze the behavior of the transducer's components interaction. This calculus model is focused on the movement of the elastic element of the shock transducer that is driven by external forces and contains a permanent magnet that produces the magnetic field needed to influence the Hall sensor. Two different types of mechanical excitation sources, rectangular and triangular, were considered. The excitation forces were applied to the transducer's support, the aim of the paper being to confer a prediction chain from mechanical movement to magnetic field fluctuation and finally to Hall voltage variation at the output of the transducer. Some constructive aspects related to the presented transducer were also presented.

articleTitle: Temperature monitoring system in automated circuit breakers
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Due to weakened electrical contacts in the interior of circuit breakers an undesired phenomenon appears which leads to unwanted effects in the global energetic system. Due to this effect in the circuit breaker, an electrical arc appears which can lead to heating of the respective material and the appearance of network harmonics, aging of materials and influence on the device's functionality. A low cost temperature measurement system in automated circuit breakers has been devised. This system can aid us in identifying the eventual problems during the functioning of the device.

articleTitle: The calculation of “F” factor and Evaluation of Radiation Emitted by UV Lamps
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In the present paper the authors propose to evaluate the level of human exposure to UV radiation by elaborating two scenarios for testing these types of lamps. In order to overcome the inconveniences created by the mathematical difficulties in calculating the emissions emitted by UV lamps, the authors have developed an “F” factoring application that they have implemented in the case of laboratory tests in parallel with the mathematical calculation. The results of the calculation of the “F” factor having an insignificant deviation, which led to the validation of the calculation application.

articleTitle: Adaptive OrCAD Simulation Approach in Teaching Non Linear Devices
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In this paper the authors present a new technique applicable for simulating fluorescent lamps considered as non-linear devices. The procedure is accurate, with less or no convergence problem encountered during the simulation. This technique is a good fit regarding teaching non-linear systems design topics at both undergraduate and graduate levels, and responds properly to demands from industry. The object of this example used for demonstration is a fluorescent lamp.

articleTitle: Lightning System of a Commercial Space in an Energy Efficiency Approach
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The high quantity of electric power used by the commercial spaces makes them suitable for energetic efficiency. Starting from the point that commercial spaces play a very prominent role in our modern society, this paper puts forward the results of a case study regarding a chain of such spaces, analyzing from a comparative standpoint the situations observed at a workstation level.

articleTitle: Case study on the Implementation of Renewable Sources in the Medium Voltage Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Distributed Generation with Renewable Energy is a vast subject and a current research on national and international level, mainly due to the high level of development of the solutions in the production of energy from renewable sources. The continuous development of the production technologies has determined in recent years the penetration of the renewable sources into the energy distribution systems in an increasing proportion, in some cases radically modifying their structure. It is proposed as a case study the modeling in the “ATP - Alternative Transients Program” of a real medium voltage distribution network and the validation of the model based on results recorded in the real network. The ATP model obtained is intended to be usable and reliable for further analysis of transient regimes.

articleTitle: Software-Defined Motor Control System in the Internet of Things Era
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The purpose of this research paper is to analyze a few ways in which numeric control of the induction motor could be brought closer to the wider Internet of Things movement of the current technical age, by using PC or PC-like machines to adjust the parameters of the motor control system in order to obtain a desired behavior.

articleTitle: Optimization of solutions for the Bus Bar Protections from ETN 220 – 400 kV
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The previous article presented at this prestigious conference proposed the use of distance protections with communication on the IEC61850 as a redundant solution to dedicated busbar protection schemes. This article demonstrates much better sensitivity of these protection schemes, which the author initially developed within the PhD thesis of the Doctoral School of the Faculty of Automatic Control and Computer, University Politehnica Bucharest.

articleTitle: Specific parameters for power plants connection to National Power System European regulation
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The elaboration of the network codes aims to ensure the technical and commercial conditions for the interconnected operation of the power systems, allowing the realization of the European common electricity market. The European Network Codes set harmonised rules for grid connection for power generating modules “in order to provide a clear legal framework for grid connections, facilitate Union-wide trade in electricity, ensure system security, facilitate the integration of renewable electricity sources, increase competition and allow more efficient use of the network and resources, for the benefit of consumers” (COMMISSION REGULATION (EU) 2016/631 of 14 April 2016 establishing a network code on requirements for grid connection of generators). Elaboration of grid codes is a great challenge for TSOs, generators and manufacturers. As the grid is constantly evolving and new technologies are incorporated to it, grid codes will have to evolve as well. Implications of any grid code parameter should be carefully studied together with cost-benefit assessment in case performance requirements are too stringent for current equipment technologies. In this paper we highlight the specific parameters that must be fulfilled by power plants in the process of connection and during operation life in the Romanian National Power System.

articleTitle: Analysis over the waveforms of the electromagnetic actuators. Adaptive-delta modulation
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper sets forth an analysis over the waveforms of the electromagnetic actuators. Due to modulation the resulted sinusoidal load current is one of the inherent drawbacks, issuing a poor response time and high losses. The following work investigates the possibility of using a particular type of modulation, which will fix the time delay problem and will decrease the losses. A potential solution to the shortcomings which occur in the case of sinusoidal modulation is the implementation of the adaptive-delta modulation, using an element with a similar behavior as the electromagnetic generator coil within the reaction loop of the modulator.

articleTitle: Advanced techniques for fault detection and classification in electrical power transmission systems: An overview
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: One of the consequences of the power systems complexity increasing consists in the rise of probability of system fault occurrence. A rapid restoration of power system enhances the service reliability and reduces power outages; therefore, fault section should be estimated quickly and accurately. Transmission lines, as important elements of power systems, may be subject to unexpected failures due to various faults. So, to guarantee the reliability and safety of a power system, efficient fault detection, classification and localization (FDL) schemes for transmission lines are essential. Consequently, the improvement in suitable techniques for the fault detection and classification (FD) in power transmission systems, to increase the efficiency of the systems and to avoid major damages, it is a permanent requirement. A lot of FD methods are described in the technical literature and proposed by a large variety of research works, so a suitable survey of these methods is needed for choosing the most proper FD technique. In this work, an overview on the methods used for FD in transmission systems is accomplished, analyzing the technical literature and summarizing the most important methods that can be applied for FD. After overall concepts and general ideas are presented, representative works are covered and discussed briefly, focusing on the newly approaches (including machine learning) developed by various researchers for FD in power transmission systems.

articleTitle: Electrical Machines Used in Electric Power Steering Applications
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: In advanced vehicles electric power steering systems owing several advantages are replacing the classical hydraulic ones. The main part of such systems is the electrical machine developing the required steering torque. The paper is a survey on the most widely used electrical machines proposed for these vital systems of a modern vehicle.

articleTitle: Energy/Cost efficiency study on V2G operating mode for EVs and PREVs
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Major vehicle manufacturers started development of Electric Vehicles (EV) and electrified powertrains, pushed by the tougher and tougher emissions constraints. The growing number of EVs led to introduction of Vehicle to Grid (V2G) concept as an instrument to reduce the load variation during a day, bringing with it a reduction of energy prices during peakload. Since the introduction of V2G concept, a number of studies have been made to estimate the benefits which this technology could bring in multiple different scenarios. In this paper, we will try to highlight one of the main obstacles because of which the V2G concept is not widespread, specifically the low energy efficiency and low economic benefits, which are coming at a high level of costs.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency and Power Quality Indicators of a Micro Grid. Case study: Lighting Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The current development of Micro - Grids, combined with the pressure enforced by national legislation as a direct effect of the Directive 2012/27/EU and the Directive 2018/844/EU leads to a new set of problems for the end-users, under the form of optimizing the Energy Efficiency (Energy Performance Indicators - EPIs) - Power Quality relationship. As it has been already proven by other studies, certain Energy Performance Improvement Actions (EPIAs) can and will influence the Power Quality Indices (PQIs) of an electrical grid. In this paper, the changes induced in the PQIs of a Micro Grid by the implementation of an EPIA regarding the lighting systems have been analyzed, in order to determine the function that would best describe the variation of the EPI - PQI relationship.

articleTitle: Energy efficiency holistic approach for new energy business model towards 2030
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Updated 2030 scenarios and climate change control actions, following the Paris accord, imply new energy investment approaches. The renewable energies and the energy efficiency measures have an essential role in energy transition. Presently, there is a need for a holistic approach of the sustainable investments that significantly contribute to the reduction of carbon footprint, giving the answers to all stakeholders and converting the project's results in relevant information for each of the involved party. The energy performance contracting model faces difficulties in facile implementation in Romania, as in other European countries, due to the disconnection between expectations of involved parties. The energy performance investment project is contributing to CO2 reduction, involves sustainability, needs legislative framework and technological development, jobs creation, comfort increase, political support, provide replication model or allow incremental implementation if the case. The present paper intends to contribute to the development of the energy efficiency contracting model in Europe proving a new approach of the energy investment projects from the perspective of all relevant stakeholders: beneficiaries, technicians, financiers, authorities, community and environmental activists. The paper propose a methodology for evaluation the performance of energy efficiency solutions to tertiary consumers based on a multi-criteria assessment built to analyze the technical, energy efficiency, environmental, economic and social impacts associated with the analyzed energy system. The proposed methodology for evaluation the performance of the energy efficiency improvement solutions will allow the development of sustainable energy efficiency projects technically and economically feasible and environment friendly to assimilate as attractive investments with priority to implementation.

articleTitle: Is there a way to become prosumer? Promoting the prosumer concept in Romania
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Prosuming-promoted in UE countries by photovoltaic plants in private households for local electricity consumption, have significant growth rates. What is the path for the development of prosumers starting up 2019 in Romania? What are the major factors that have influenced national prosumer in UE between 1990-2018, support schemes, regulatory provisions, information and third-party markets, under conditions with different national policy factors? How policy shapes the role of residential PV prosumer paradigms? In Romania, investment in residential photovoltaic installations will be sustainable if there are government subsidies for local production and consumption and for isolated, non-electrical, hybrid solutions. The decision criteria will be influenced by four factors: technical, economic, environmental and socio-political. Reducing fees for approvals will be important factors in promoting renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: Aspects on Harmonics Analytical Identification of a Periodic Non-Sinusoidal Wave
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Multiple fields of science and social life use representations of time variations for physical, chemical, biological, statistical variables. When the representation of these variables versus time is periodic, the use of the discrete Fourier transform to identify harmonics and continuous components represents an immediate solution, favored by the affordability of data acquisition and computer assistance. Research over the past two decades has highlighted some major aspects in the field of harmonic composition identification of periodic non-sinusoidal waves, such as the alternative current “alias” phenomenon, the maximum harmonic order that can be determined by discrete Fourier transform, as well as the possibility of appearance of the direct current “alias” phenomenon, i.e. on the continuous component of the analyzed wave. This work has three objectives related to the analytical identification of a periodic non-sinusoidal wave harmonics. Firstly, it is determined a system of three equations, of which a transcendent one, based on which the three unknown parameters of a harmonic are calculated: the amplitude, the order and the phase. Initial data are represented by the coordinates of three different points. The second aspect approached is represented by the harmonic analysis of a periodic non-sinusoidal wave with a finite number of harmonics and highlighting the manifestation modalities of alias phenomena. Finally, the third objective deals with the use of an odd number of samples over a period, a case so far avoided due to a small simplification in writing the computational relationships, but which may occur frequently due to the frequency variations at the fundamental level (such as in power systems).

articleTitle: Simulating the mobile network behavior by applying DTN in ONE simulator of the use case of a real town communication
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The usage of Delay Tolerant Networks in mobile ad-hoc networks is very useful in different difficult situations where traditional routing techniques can not be applied in order to establish and maintain the continuous communication between the nodes. The different features that DTN allow you to simulate the real town mobile networks and information exchange between two neighbor nodes in case where the nodes keep moving by following the street and lanes of a real town map, and while nodes keep changing their behavior and state too. The simulation environment of ONE simulator allows to configure a platform that depict and helps to test the DTN protocols. The study consists on applying the DTN protocols in ONE simulator for a real town in Albania where some conclusions came out by estimating the overall network performance.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of the Three-Phase Induction Motor Operating in Conditions of Unbalanced Voltage Supply
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper uses analytical, numerical and experimental procedures for investigating several effects of the unbalanced voltage supply on the motor performance. The analytical electrical model of the induction motor (IM), developed for positive and negative sequence is an appropriate instrument for the evaluation of the IM operation in conditions of unbalanced power supply. This model brings a coherent procedure for the calculating the unbalanced current, losses of each category, respectively the developed torque. Data from analytical calculations became input for numerical analysis of the motor using the Finite Element Method (FEM). The induction motor performance evaluation through experiments is meant to compare the predicted results and complete the investigation. Finally, the work comes with recommendations regarding the eventual rerating as well as protective equipment set-up.

articleTitle: Graduate skills for the Power Engineering sector: On the match between supply and demand
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Higher Education Institutions have been up-skilling learners and preparing them for employment since the first University was established in 859AD in Fez, Morocco. The education process is a matching process of skills between what the learner wants and what employers require. To be effective this matching process requires both parties to understand what skills are required, to have a common understanding of the skills and how to articulate them and in how competence in them are verified. Traditionally Higher Education programmes have had a focus on developing technical skills. In Engineering programmes this typically involves establishing a solid foundation in understanding of Mathematics, in the principles of how objects interact with their environment, design and development of system components and systems, how to fabricate and test and how to professionally document work. Industry is increasingly expressing the need for softer skills, variously called generic, transferable, employability and skills for life. This paper shows the place of technical and generic skills in the employment transition by presenting a generic model for the transition from education into employment and looks at some example skills from UK power engineering job adverts to illustrate the definitional and warranting issues. The adverts show that employers use some very high-level skills constructs in their requirements for new recruits and very general adjectives to describe the required competence in these skills. The skill requirements, as indicated by the label used to define them, whilst overlapping with the skills being embedded into education programmes do not align closely. Further, and potentially more worryingly, the statement of the degree of competence in the skills do not align at all with the methods of measurement of competence in the skills even where such measurements exist. The paper concludes with some general comments and recommendations for ways forward.

articleTitle: Methodology for the sizing of a hybrid energy storage system in low voltage distribution grids
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper presents a methodology for the sizing of hybrid storage solutions in low-voltage distribution networks. A hybrid storage solution is defined as that able to integrate and maximize the performance of a heterogeneous grouping of battery types. The methodology relays on a step-by-step analysis of field data collected from the area at which the hybrid solution is intended to be connected to. It also considers diverse restrictions related to available budget, technical constraints related to the different technologies included, and business and future exploitation aspects. A study case based on a real demonstration is presented to validate the proposed methodology.

articleTitle: On Circuit Analysis and Simulation of Networks with Nullors
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: This paper describes the new modeling of nullor-based active devices from the circuit abstraction level. After a brief overview of the nullor concept and its properties, follows a detailed description regarding the modeling of active devices in the voltage-mode, current-mode, respectively in the mixed mode of operation. This modeling description reflects the two-port and four-terminal network point of view. Simulation of the four nullor-controlled types of sources, as well as modeling of the multiport circuit elements, requires the development of suitable equivalent circuits constructed using bipolar circuit elements and the nullor. Studying the behavior of such a circuit, voltage and current wise, require its association with two graphs: one current graph namely Gi, for the systematic formulation of the 1st Kirchhoff's Theorem, and one voltage graph called Gv, for the systematic formulation of the 2nd Kirchhoff's Theorem. The use of the two graphs in the analog analysis applied to circuits with nullors implies the elaboration of efficient algorithms, implemented in specialized software, capable of generating voltage and current graphs automatically. Considering the nullator an over-determined two-port circuit element (zero voltage, zero current) whereas the norator is an undetermined two-port circuit element (any voltage and any current), this paper presents the way of formulating equations of all kinds, straight from the diagrams of the functional circuits containing nullors. Existing simulation software may be applied to simulate the nullor having an ideal voltage-controlled voltage source, ec = Ac_c uc, with an ideal independent current source, jC=0.0 A used for gate control and possessing a substantial amplification (transfer) factor Ac_C. Therefore, all types of equations, which describe functional circuits have a simple formulation, no matter the presence of nullors. In this way, it becomes possible to elaborate efficient algorithms applicable for the automatic formulation of Kirchhoff's equations, loop equations, modified nodal equations and state equations for circuits with nullors as well. The example presented here pleaded for the validity of the nullor modeling.

articleTitle: Diagnostic and Input Selection Tool applied on Weather Variables for Studies of Short-Term Load Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: One of the main studies applied on Operation Planning is short-term load forecasting, which results are obtained mainly by hour in few days ahead horizon. The load forecasting model quality is directly related to two factors, the definition of the input variables of the forecasting model and the mathematical modeling of this model. About the first aspect, the most significant exogenous influences on demand in the short-term load forecasting horizon are the weather variables, mainly temperature, humidity and wind speed. Regardless of the weather variable considered, it is necessary to perform a correlation study of the influence of this variable on demand, in each different region and climatic season. Thus, the objective of this work is to present a study of feature selection related to weather variables considering the application of a short-term load forecasting model to four different climate zones. This study, based on a feature selection tool that generates results of relation between the demand and the weather variables, aims to justify the definition of different weather inputs for each region, seeking to increase the quality of the load forecasting results. Also, the feature selection tool is based on different math definitions, that contributes to a better pattern recognition.

articleTitle: Energy efficiency evaluation method of low and medium voltage distribution systems to industrial consumers
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Nowadays, financial constraints are those that dictate the behavior in the national economy. Thus, optimizing energy costs and increasing energy efficiency in industrial installations can be a trigger for increasing the economic performance of the industrial unit. This paper presents a minimalist but sufficient and pertinent approach for power analysis in low and medium voltage distribution installations belonging to the industrial consumers, summarizing the observations from real energy audits carried out on more than one hundred industrial enterprises in Romania during last years. The paper synthesizes the main elements required for power analysis of and proposes relevant indicators to be evaluated for a correct assessment of the energy performance measures as decision base for stakeholders to support the investment for energy efficiency projects of the industrial unit. Improving energy efficiency is not only the reason for economic growth of industrial consumers, but on macroeconomic level it is a priority of national energy policy due to its contribution to achieving power security, sustainable development and competitiveness of industry, saving primary energy resources and reducing gas emissions with greenhouse effect.

Author Keywords: low and medium voltage distribution system

articleTitle: Knowledge-based system for the analysis of voltage fluctuations and flicker
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Voltage fluctuations of low frequency that can cause light flicker are a power quality issue that affects several parts of the national distribution networks. In the most cases the flicker indices exceed the standards-imposed thresholds and the source of disturbance is unknown, thus becoming a troublesome situation. Considering these aspects, a knowledge-based system prototype was developed. It is dedicated to analyzing the voltage disturbances that occur in distribution networks, mainly voltage fluctuations. The paper presents the power quality issue of voltage fluctuations and flicker and the proposed artificial intelligence system.

articleTitle: Integrating the industrial consumer into smart grid by load curve forecasting using machine learning
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: Integration of industrial consumers into the smart grid concept can be facilitated by optimizing short and very short-term forecasts of load curves for industrial consumers. Minimizing forecast errors can improve the supplier-consumer relationship by reducing supplier balancing costs, which can lower the energy bill, and anticipate possible network faults or network congestion which means improved operation across the entire power system. The present paper aims at demonstrating the usefulness of energy forecasting by using machine learning methods. In the context of installing monitoring systems with load curve recording data at short intervals of time, huge amounts of data are obtained that need to be capitalized in real time (automated), otherwise the investments necessary to modernize the way in which the energy is used are not justified, consequently disfavouring the development and digitization of electrical networks. Integration of the industrial consumer into the smart grid concept can be applied in detail at large industrial consumers where forecasts can be made on certain areas inside factories or electric equipment with high installed electric capacity. The use of smart grid technologies removes the current limits for monitoring, processing and communication between consumption and production. To be able to capitalize on the forecasts, a very important aspect is the automation of their realization and quick access to the decision makers who may be human or other smart grid integrated systems. That is why the present paper proposes the use of machine learning methods in the short and very short forecast, and the results will be compared with the classical forecasting methods. Hourly load curves from the industrial consumers will be used for forecasts.

articleTitle: A scheduling optimization model of electric water heaters for electricity cost minimization with limited information
publicationTitle: 2019 8th International Conference on Modern Power Systems (MPS)
abstract: The present paper defines the equations that govern the optimization model of an electric water heater in order to manage automatically its available flexibility for the user's own benefit. A case study that focuses on the electric water heater flexibility potential is carried out: it is aimed to minimize the total expected electricity cost of a single household that only has an electric water heater as a flexibility source. The temperature inside the hot water tank is an unknown value since the temperature sensor is not sending any information outside. Moreover, real hot water consumption is uncertain and the model takes decisions based on forecasting models. Given the limited information available, the model is developed in a conservative way with the objective of maintaining both, the hot water temperature and the user's comfort. The results show that it is possible to reduce the electricity bill by managing optimally the available flexibility from the electric water heater.
